tips.text: Dip cold noodles into tasty thick hot soup, this is tsukemen! Free soup refill. If your soup gets cold, ask for the spectacular soup heating iron.
Huge delicious udon noodles. If you are very hungry, ask for twice or triple serving, it is free! Great udon, comfy atmosphere, but expect to wait 20 minutes before getting a seat.
A lunchtime legend. Pad thai special on Thursdays (¥980) is divine.
Sushi place. Set menus are available, and their ¥3000 lunch set is excellent. Dress code: No sleeveless for men.

This complex of six restaurants on the sixth floor is a good choice if price is not an issue. You can choose between sushi, steak, Japanese and Chinese, and will be looking at upwards of ¥5000 per head on the bill.
Described as somewhat of a hidden gem, this three Michelin star restaurant run by renowned "sushi maestro" Takashi Saito. With just eight seats, reservations should be made early.
A superb food section in the basement with enough free samples to make a full lunch, if you don't mind not having a place to sit.

Kinoshita makes eating French food in Japan justifiable. Some say that with its underpriced menu, dinner courses for ¥3800-¥7000, and weekday lunches for ¥1800, this restaurant is considered one of the best kept secrets in Tokyo. But in fact it is popular, and reservations are mandatory. Menu in French and Japanese.
tips.hours: 12:00-14:00, 18:00-21:00, closed Mondays and the third Tue of each month

tips.text: Although it is Shibuya in terms of address, it is a udon store closer to Shinjuku. It is cost-effective and features homemade udon noodles.

Tucked away among Korean hostess bars, a cozy joint with some of the most authentic Mexican food you're likely to find in Japan -- the owner makes regular trips to Mexico. Excellent selection of tequilas, home-made tortillas, and lucha libre wrestling masks for guests.

The name means "essence of milk", a reference to the Buddha's highest teachings, and this restaurant aims for the highest standards of shōjin-ryori (精進料理), the purely vegetarian version of Japan's refined kaiseki cuisine. Located within the grounds of the Seishōji temple, all meals here are elaborate, ten-course affairs served in private rooms with a view of the lovely temple garden. With dinner courses priced at ¥15,000-19,000 per person (plus drinks, tax and service), the experience doesn't come cheap, but it just might be worth it for an unforgettable occasion — and this is still only a third of what Ginza's kaiseki joints charge. Reservations obligatory.
Okonomiyaki cooked at your table.
A good place for Thai street-stall style food. It's always packed and hectic for lunch, with attendants hollering to attract customers.
Pizza and pasta restaurant. The building is full of restaurants all run by Sapporo Beer.
Authentic Turkish food. HALAL food.
Excellent traditional but modern Japanese restaurant. Plenty of dishes to order but you need to like leeks.

Rotating (kaiten) wanko soba, the Iwate tradition of eating soba one mouthful per small bowl: here the bowls circle a standing counter and you take as many as you like in 40 minutes. A patch at 100 bowls, a gold patch at 200 and a gold medal at 300. Standing only, no chairs; English-speaking staff. No phone reservations; walk-ins are served in order of arrival.
tips.price: ¥3,800 for 40 minutes, all you can eat

tips.text: Specializing in the infamous fugu (blowfish), it's one of the huge number of seafood restaurants in Kabukichō (see below). Set dinners go for around ¥5000, featuring fugu prepared five or six ways, fresh from the tank. Has another branch nearby (at 1-3-15 Kabukicho).

One of Tokyo's oldest chanko joints, operating for over 100 years, specializing in a slightly unusual miso-flavored soup. Lunch sets at ¥840/1260 weekdays/weekends are just about the cheapest chanko you'll find anywhere and a good option for the solo traveller. Dinner starts from ¥2940/person for the Tomoegata (miso) or Yahazuyama (dashi) set and goes up to ¥8400 for the aptly humongous 9-course Yokozuna.
Great coffee and delicious sandwiches, with a warm smile.

This is a fashionable cafe of Paris style. You can enjoy elegant mood with seeing a row of houses and street of Omotesando. You can also choose fish or meat for lunch. Has another branch at Minato Mirai in Yokohama.
Antenna shop of Izu Islands and Ogasawara Islands.
Truely classic kissaten (full-service coffee shop).
Japanese sweets and drinks. Famous for dorayaki, drum-shaped cake with red-bean paste inside.
Specialty coffee from northern Thailand.

This maid cafe has card games, drinks, food, and young women dressed up as maids to serve you. If you order an omelet, they'll draw a picture of a cute animal on the top in ketchup. In addition to this shop, there are 3 branch stores elsewhere in Akihabara.

A 'cat cafe': you play with the shop's (very clean) cats while drinking tea. You'll be asked to remove your shoes and wash your hands on entry. You'll also be gently pressured to order one of their drinks. It's a different experience.
tips.price: ¥500 for first 30 minutes; ¥150 for each ten minutes; drinks ¥300 to ¥500

tips.text: The original and not quite as over-the-top (or expensive) as some of the competition. A long line can form on weekends.
A statue of an owl (fukurō) near the east exit. Many people use this as a meeting spot.
A cigar bar that serves coffee, alcoholic drinks, and desserts. There is a large cigar selection, in particular from the Dominican Republic.

Ludicrously fluffy pancakes served in wobbly stacks of three, with a selection of sweet and savoury toppings. Extremely popular among the Instagram crowd, the only way to get a guaranteed seat is to queue up in person before 8:30am and pay a ¥1000/person deposit. No English sign, but English menu available.
Freshly grilled taiyaki, a traditional sweet waffle in the shape of a lucky fish, with your choice of red bean, sweet potato or custard filling.
This place has been making "melon pan" since 1945, and they haven't changed the decoration. It is a buttery and milky small cake with a crispy sweet crust.

info.note: classical music tea/coffee place, no talking

tips.text: This restaurant/cafe often holds events including guest speakers and live shows. The hamburger menu is popular.

Popular with business people or singles during lunchtime. Meal sets are ¥980–1200, comes w/ main, salad, drink; main being spaghetti, etc. Useful for a late night spot to hang around, since they're open until 06:00.
Jazzy cafe with 1960s decor in moody lighting. Excellent food, try the quiche, although portions are small.
Cruisy open-air bar with a torii gate at the entrance. Crowd spilling onto the street makes it feel like a block party.

Founded by a Tokyo resident returning from abroad. Located across the Sumida river from the Asakusa tourist district. Clientele has many expats and English-speaking Japanese. Periodically hosts an English-language comedy show.
The only Japanese antenna of the Scottish franchise, this bar has twenty different European and Japanese craft beers on tap.

Serves a selection of Aussie lagers including VB, Crown Lager and Coopers, cocktails and meat pies. A big-screen TV and a wide range of music played by DJs provide ongoing entertain­ment. You can also kick back Australian-style along the U-shaped bar.
It is a sushi restaurant located in Shibuya, but close to Shinjuku Station. The lunch special features cost-effectiveness.
Primarily lesbian bar with all-female staff, and karaoke for the multinational patrons. Interior themed like a 1970s motel. Saturday is strictly women-only; Monday is FtM night.
Bar with dancefloor known for attracting bisexual crowds.

Full of lotus flowers and waterfowl and has the picturesque little Bentendō Hall shrine, dedicated to the goddess Benzaiten, in the middle. Outside the main entrance of the temple is a statue of Ugajin, a Japanese folk god of harvests, fertility, and wealth who is represented as a coiled serpent with a bearded man’s head.

The home of the Denki Bran cocktail, this was Japan's first Western-style bar when it first opened in 1880 and remains a truly local institution. The ground floor is a large beer-hall-like bar, the second is a Western-style restaurant, and the upper floor serves Japanese food. Find a seat at one of the shared tables, buy your tickets at the counter, and join in the fun. Beware the oddly limited operating hours: last order is 19:30!
Small, decent bar with NYC pop radio. Attracts a nice mix of tourists, expats and locals. A really welcome respite from the overpriced and overrated bars in the surrounding area.

Up a flight of stairs to the left of TGI Friday's. No cover except for special events, drinks are reasonable and the staff is English friendly. Popular among expats for its smaller size and music selection, you can often find groups or solo western businessmen (and women) on expense accounts into the wee hours of the morning. Does get crowded at times, so go early if you actually want enough space to dance.

An appropriately grubby joint decorated with propaganda posters and booming bass, playing mostly recent hits. While best known for its shots (check out the leaderboards!), their other drinks are pretty decent too and they have quite a selection of American whiskeys. The friendly staff parties as hard as the customers.
tips.price: Drinks ¥800–1000 (half price before 21:00), no cover charge

tips.text: Dance music, plays the top hits of the moment.
Hip-hop, R&B, and reggae club.
Mix of hip-hop and techno. one of the most popular after hours nightclubs open from 22:00 until 12:00 the next day
Specializing in old-school funk/soul/disco. Put on your platform soles, comb your 'fro, and boogie on back to 1979.

Multi-room nightclub that plays a mix of hip-hop, r&b, and techno/house in their different areas. Most of the clientele is of a younger crowd (ages 20-25). Friday's entrance fee is only ¥1000 (including two drinks).
Owned by Vanilla, this club houses three dance floors with music ranging from psychedelic trance to hip-hop.
tips.price: Entrance fee is only ¥1000 before midnight

tips.text: Popular for trance music all night long.
Large two-floor all hip-hop club. Foreigners may not be admitted unless they bring along a Japanese friend.
tips.price: ¥3000, occasional discount if you enter before midnight

tips.text: One of Tokyo's largest clubs, designed by the people behind New York's Twilo and the setting of a scene in Babel.
A two level nightclub and lounge with a large dance floor and darts. The DJ normally spins hip-hop, R&B, reggae, and house, and there are live house performances periodically through the night.

Performance art space meets bar run with a simple concept: different people and groups rent a block of time and do whatever they want to. The end result runs from stand-up comedy and lectures to porn star photo shoots and incredibly violent live S&M. Erotic shows 18+ only (ID required).
Small bar full of men. It's not easy to find, so call for directions.
Among Nichō's most well-known pubs, with a thumping dance floor. A hand stamp upon entry will also get you into sister bar The Annex.
"Mix bar". Has another branch at Shibuya PARCO.
Masculine gay pub with a dance floor. Rebuilt after a fire, the place is popular among male and female foreigners, and with Japanese men.
Relaxed basement bar with somewhat more mature crowds.

Tucked away in this tiny cubbyhole of a space is one of the most interesting small bars in Tokyo. A country western theme with Chet Baker and Nat King Cole pouring from the stereo. The food is cheap and superbly done (think chili nachos and the like); beer and spirits are also available. The place is tiny but it attracts a great mix of young groups of friends and office workers. Some nights Marone puts on live music and cover charges are upwards of ¥4000! The older couple who run the bar are terrifically friendly but their English is minimal.

Toyosu is new home of the world's largest wholesale market for seafood and produce after its relocation from Tsukiji. Unlike the old facility where tourists could almost walk up to the fish, Toyosu's market has large enclosed observation decks and dedicated paths for tourists to view the action, including the famous tuna auctions. However, early morning fish sales start before public transit opens, so take a taxi for those.
tips.hours: Mon-Sat 05:00-17:00; closed holidays and most Wednesdays

info.note: 千代田区役所に入る図書館です。

tips.text: The lavish government building for the Bunkyo ward of Tokyo, once described in the Japan Times as "a colossal Pez candy dispenser." A free observation deck on the 25th floor, jutting out of the top like the Starship Enterprise, commands a fine view of much of Tokyo.

This busy covered shopping arcade leads from the Kaminarimon gate to the temple, selling all sorts of Buddhist paraphernalia as well as assorted tourist kitsch. This is one of the best places in Tokyo to buy souvenirs (the other being the Oriental Bazaar in Omotesando), but more expensive items such as swords and kimono are likely to be of inferior quality. Slightly nicer crafts, rather than mass-produced kitsch, can be found at good prices if you walk up to the temple, turn right, and turn right again on the first small street running parallel to Nakamise. You will see plenty of small shops in this general area which have better quality souvenirs and gifts, like handkerchiefs, strings of hand-made silk balls, and hairclips.

info.note: Magnet mall's park rooftop Shibuya Crossing observation deck; charges for access

info.chain: ヒューマントラストシネマ

info.note: 月見テラスの水盤内に設置された、細長い彫刻的な石造オブジェ。かつて月見の名所であった歴史的な高輪の海岸風景に浮かぶ船をイメージしており、水面に浮かぶサーフボードのようにも見える。背景には東京の街並みが広がる。
六本木ヒルズ・けやき坂通りのクリスマスイルミネーション
銀座に残された唯一の鉄道踏切信号機

世界自然遺産に登録された奄美大島、加計呂麻島を東京に再現。
子どもの幸せを願う神社、龍神様ををお祀りしている潮見 『龍宮社』。
伊勢丹新宿店・屋上庭園

伊勢丹の創業者
伊勢丹新宿店・屋上庭園
伝統的な日本文化とハイエネルギーのパフォーマンスを組み合わせた東京の活気あるディナーショーです。食事は二の次ですが、熱心なパフォーマーと賑やかな雰囲気が必見の体験を生み出します。
1989年に東京駅八重洲口近くに設置された安藤泉の金属製キリンの彫刻。高さ6.25mで、伝統的な中国医学の王としてのキリンを象徴する冠をかぶっており、元の設置場所である津村ビルを示している。

Rozan (廬山, Lu Shan) is a famous mountain in Jiangxi, China, celebrated in Chinese poetry and painting.
Designers created a miniature version of Rozan using:
a small artificial hill, stone arrangements &  plantings that evoke Chinese landscape aesthetics
復刻道標(右 いも坂みち 左 ねぎしみち)
伊東 深水（いとう しんすい、1898年（明治31年）2月4日 - 1972年（昭和47年）5月8日）は、大正・昭和期の浮世絵師、日本画家、版画家。本名、一（はじめ）。実娘は女優・タレント・歌手の朝丘雪路。
famous for the Ako incident (47 ronin attack)
2015年 生理学・医学賞の理学博士 大村智先生の記念碑

famous gold-colored statue located in Tokyo's Kappabashi Kitchen Town. Erected in 2003 to commemorate the 90th anniversary of the shopping district and honor the legend of a local merchant named Kihachi Kappaya, who was said to be helped by river kappas.

銀座「蕎麦の花」内、2013/5/31-6/29 限定オープン

フォークロアでは、伝統的な日本の飲料である日本酒や焼酎を、ブルーチーズブランデーを加えた焼酎マティーニなどの革新的なカクテルに再構築しています。バーカウンターのミニマリストな内装は、佐野文彦スタジオによって日本各地の寺院から調達された歴史的な素材を使用してデザインされており、静かな雰囲気を生み出し、ゲストが日本のミクソロジーの豊かな文化遺産を尊重しながら、ドリンクメニューの芸術性を十分に楽しむことができるようになっています。
この銀座の地下バーは、上野秀嗣の氷彫刻技術で知られ、日本のバーテンダー技術とクラシックレシピを組み合わせており、オープン以来、世界の50ベストバーリストに名を連ねています。 'ホワイトレディ'や日本限定の'フルブルーム'などのシグネチャーカクテルを提供し、2019年にはアジアの50ベストで日本のベストバーに選ばれましたが、その人気のため予約をお勧めします。
東京の銀座タワー10階に位置するブルガリバー銀座は、豪華なイタリアンラウンジ体験を提供し、素晴らしい景色とクラシックなカクテルやオリジナルの創作カクテルを楽しめます。ゲストはイタリアン風のバー料理やアフタヌーンティーボックスを味わい、屋上のオープンエア「ラ・テラス・ドン・ペリニヨン」も探索できます。
